newsitem.title: ITALY: PRESS DIGEST - Italy - Thursday May 29.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Italy - Thursday May 29.

text.p: Following are some of the top headlines in leading Italian newspapers.
* Deputy prime minister Walter Veltroni said the government would approve the three-year economic programme known as the DPEF at a cabinet meeting on Friday (all).
* The senate (upper house) approved the government's 1997 mini-budget including 15.5 trillion lire of deficit-cutting measures which will now become law (all).

* Prime minister Romano Prodi will meet trade union leaders in order to discuss further details of the DPEF. Unions do not like the government's deficit cutting measures programme, deriving two thirds of deficit reduction from welfare and public spending cuts and one third from increased revenues (all).

* Italian bourse regulator said control of privatised companies should not be protected by measures which limit the role of the stock market. Consob also said it approved the principle of stable shareholding cores as long as these did not signify an unlimited guarantee of the maintenance of control. Consob also said San Paolo bank's stock offering was in line with privatisation rules and saw no need for the holding of Italy's biggest bank to carry out a public share purchase (all).
* Italian foreign exchange office said the country's overall balance of payments recorded a 2.144 trillion lire deficit in April (Sole 24 Ore).

* The Agnelli family holding company IFI said its 1996 consolidated attributable net profit rose to 447 billion lire against 411 billion in 1995. The group also said it would raise 1996 dividends on ordinary and privilege shares by 40 lire per share to 440 lire and 490 lire respectively (all).
* A report by national statistics institute Istat showed employment in Italian industrial firms with more than 500 employers fell 3.9 percent year-on-year in February (Sole 24 Ore).
Reuters has not verified these stories and cannot vouch for their accuracy.
